title: Hardware firmware compatibility and telemetry specification for private deployments
author: Priya Kumar
body:
Purpose
-------
This document defines the hardware, firmware and telemetry requirements for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem appliance variants). It prescribes the supported hardware matrix, firmware baselines, the telemetry agent specification, network endpoints, privacy controls, SLOs for telemetry delivery, and step-by-step verification and rollback guidance for enabling telemetry on customer clusters. The intent is to provide a single reference the SRE, Solutions, and On‑Prem teams can rely on during onboarding and Day‑2 operations.

Scope
-----
- Applies to private (VPC and on‑prem) deployments of Redwood inference control plane and serving nodes.
- Covers firmware and BIOS/UEFI baselines for supported GPUs/CPUs, NICs, and storage controllers.
- Specifies the redwood-telemetry agent configuration, allowed telemetry schema, retention/obfuscation requirements, and secure transport.
- Does NOT cover host OS hardening (see onprem packaging hardening doc) or cloud-provider-specific NIC driver tuning (see reference-architectures).

Summary of changes in this revision (2026-01-15)
------------------------------------------------
- Added AMD MI300X and NVIDIA H30 firmware baselines
- Introduced telemetry v2 schema and new privacy-preserving hashing for container IDs
- Tightened TLS requirements and removed legacy HTTP fallback
- New verification steps and sample systemd unit for redwood-telemetryd

Supported hardware and firmware baselines
--------------------------------------
The following table is the supported hardware matrix and minimum firmware drivers for private deployments accepted for onboarding. Customers may request exemptions via the SRE onboarding checklist but exemptions require a compatibility test and SLA addendum.

| Class | Component | Minimum firmware/driver | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| GPU | NVIDIA A100 (PCIe) | NVIDIA driver 530.41+, CUDA 12.0+ | Recommend HBM2 health checks during preflight |
| GPU | NVIDIA H100 | NVIDIA driver 545.x+, CUDA 12.1+ | Verify MIG config if used |
| GPU | NVIDIA H30 | NVIDIA driver 560.x+ (H30 firmware 1.2.0+) | New as of 2025 Q4; requires kernel 6.2+ |
| GPU | AMD MI300X | ROCm 6.0+ | Requires firmware 2.1.3+ for power-scope telemetry |
| NIC | Mellanox CX-7 | OFED 6.0+ | RDMA recommended for inter-node KV cache sync |
| NIC | Broadcom NetX 25G | BCM driver 1.9+ | Check SR-IOV stability tests |
| Storage | NVMe controllers (Enterprise) | Firmware 5.x+ | Ensure SMART passthrough enabled

Preflight checklist (operator tasks)
----------------------------------
1. Inventory: run the hardware-inventory tool on each host: rwinf-tool hw-inventory --json > /tmp/hw.json. Confirm GPU/NIC/Storage models.
2. Firmware baseline: ensure firmware/driver versions match or exceed the table above.
   - Example: sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv
3. Kernel: use kernel >= 6.0 for H100/H30 and >=5.15 for A100.
4. Disk: verify nvme SMART passthrough: sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
5. Boot mode: UEFI boot with Secure Boot optional; if Secure Boot enabled, sign redwood-bootloader modules per packaging guide.
6. Networking: confirm port access for telemetry (see Network and endpoints).
7. Time: NTP or PTP must be configured and accurate within 500ms across nodes.

Telemetry agent specification (redwood-telemetryd v2)
---------------------------------------------------
Overview: redwood-telemetryd is a lightweight, user-space agent that collects a small, curated set of host and runtime metrics, event logs, and periodic health snapshots for the Redwood control plane. The agent is designed to be privacy-conscious and can operate in a push-only mode to customer-controlled collectors.

Minimum capabilities:
- Host metrics: CPU/memory, per-GPU utilization, GPU temperature, PCIe errors, NIC errors, disk SMART summary.
- Runtime metrics: per-node process counts (redwood-runtime, redis, envoy), KV cache hit/miss counters, open connections, and RPC latencies.
- Events: GPU ECC events, node reboots, OOMs, driver module reloads.
- Snapshots: periodic config-hash, firmware versions, iptables state (optional).

Telemetry schema (v2) — allowed fields
- node_id (hashed) — SHA256 hex, salted with customer-salt
- node_role — controller | serving | gateway
- timestamp — RFC3339
- metrics.cpu.* — percent and absolute
- metrics.gpu.{index}.utilization
- metrics.gpu.{index}.temperature_c
- metrics.nic.{name}.err_packets
- events.type — e.g. ECC_ERROR, DRIVER_RELOAD
- events.detail — free text limited to 1024 chars (redacted per privacy rules)

Privacy and data minimization rules
----------------------------------
- No raw container IDs, full process command lines, or unredacted user content should be sent.
- Container IDs, hostnames, and MACs MUST be hashed using the provided per-customer salt before transmission. See hashing policy below.
- If customers opt for collector-side-only mode, the agent will emit to a local directory in encrypted format rather than outbound network.

Hashing policy for identifiers
- Use SHA256 with per-customer salt stored in /etc/redwood/customer-salt (0600).
- Example: echo -n "$SALT:$IDENT" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1

Network and endpoints
---------------------
Strict TLS 1.2+ is required for any outbound telemetry. The agent supports two transport modes:
- Managed: push to Redwood private ingestion endpoints over mTLS (for dedicated/private-managed accounts).
- Collector-proxy: push to customer-managed collector (HTTPS or gRPC) inside customer's VPC.

Required ports (egress from nodes):
- 443 TCP to allowed collector endpoint (managed or customer).
- 123 UDP NTP to customer NTP pool.

mTLS certificate rotation
- When using managed mode, certificate rotation is handled by the Private control plane over a TLS tunnel. For collector-proxy mode, customers must provide a PKCS#12 bundle updated before expiry; the Agent checks expiry at startup.

Configuration example (agent YAML)
--------------------------------
# /etc/redwood/telemetry.yaml
mode: collector-proxy
collector_url: https://collector.internal.acme.local:8443/v2/telemetry
tls:
  verify: true
  ca_bundle: "/etc/pki/ca/collector-ca.pem"
customer_salt_file: "/etc/redwood/customer-salt"
collection_interval_seconds: 30
metrics_filters:
  include: ["metrics.gpu.*","metrics.cpu.*","events.*"]
  redact_text_fields: true

Enabling the agent (systemd unit example)
----------------------------------------
Create /etc/systemd/system/redwood-telemetryd.service:
[Unit]
Description=Redwood Telemetry Agent
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/redwood-telemetryd --config /etc/redwood/telemetry.yaml
Restart=on-failure
User=root

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Enable and start:
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now redwood-telemetryd

Verification and test procedures
--------------------------------
1. Agent health: sudo systemctl status redwood-telemetryd -> Active: active (running).
2. Heartbeat event: journalctl -u redwood-telemetryd -u show | grep HEARTBEAT -> Expect heartbeat every 30s.
3. Sample payload check (local): sudo rwinf-tool telemetry-dump --last 1 -> prints JSON with hashed node_id and metrics.gpu entries.
4. End-to-end: curl -k -X POST to test collector (managed customers can request a pre-signed endpoint) and expect 200/ACK.
5. Behavioral tests: simulate driver reload: sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia and verify event ECC/DRIVER_RELOAD emitted and visible in the collector UI within 30s.

SLOs and retention
------------------
- Telemetry delivery SLO (managed mode): 99% of heartbeats delivered within 45s.
- Agent restart SLI: median restart recovery time < 60s.
- Retention (managed): raw telemetry retained 90 days; aggregated metrics retained 365 days.
- For customer-managed collectors, retention is per customer policy; Redwood requires that PII-free telemetry be kept at least 30 days for regression analysis unless otherwise contracted.

Upgrade and rollback considerations
----------------------------------
When upgrading redwood-telemetryd and/or kernel/NVIDIA drivers: the following sequence is recommended to minimize risk.
1. Canary: upgrade telemetry on 1 serving node in canary AZ, observe 10 minutes of metrics and event flows.
2. Driver upgrade: schedule driver/firmware upgrade on canary node (if required), reboot node and verify agent reconnects.
3. Scale rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 100% using configuration management tool (Ansible/Terraform provider for private).
4. Rollback triggers: if agent heartbeats drop below 90% of baseline or we observe >5% nodes with GPU ECC events post-upgrade, pause and rollback.

Rollback procedure (quick)
- Use inventory: rwinf-tool list-nodes --filter canary > canary.json
- Revert package: sudo apt-get install redwood-telemetryd=1.4.2-0 (example)
- Restart agent and verify canary health.

Troubleshooting (common issues)
-------------------------------
- Agent fails to start with 'tls: certificate expired': check /var/log/redwood-telemetryd.log, rotate certificate: sudo redwood-ctl cert-rotate --agent
- Hashed node_id mismatch: ensure /etc/redwood/customer-salt present and identical across nodes for consistent hashes.
- High telemetry latency: verify MTU/Path MTU, disable TCP segmentation offload on NIC for debugging: sudo ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off

Ownership and runbooks
----------------------
- Onboarding ownership: eng-private-deployments solutions team (owner: Miguel Santos) handles preflight approval.
- Day-2 ownership: eng-sre is primary for operational incidents.
- Runbook links: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/onprem-vpc-day2-automation-and-upgrade-playbook-2025

Customer opt-out and privacy controls
------------------------------------
Customers may opt out of managed telemetry and run collector-proxy or local-only modes. When opting out, Redwood requires a signed data-minimization agreement and an operations contact for emergency telemetry-on requests (SLA dependent).

Appendices
---------
Appendix A — Example rwinf-tool commands
1) Inventory: rwinf-tool hw-inventory --format json > /tmp/hw.json
2) Sample payload dump: rwinf-tool telemetry-dump --last 1 --pretty
3) Health check: rwinf-tool agent-health --node node-01

Appendix B — Contact escalation matrix
- Tier 1: Solutions Onboarding (oncall) — solutions-oncall@redwood.ai
- Tier 2: Eng SRE — eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai
- Tier 3: Eng Platform (telemetry runtime) — telemetry-runtime@redwood.ai

If you are planning an on‑prem deployment and need a preflight check performed by Redwood, file a request via the private-deploy-onboarding form and attach rwinf-tool hw-inventory output.
